  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Model-based means and NB mid-P transport}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}

---

ComBat-refQL 0.3.2 fits raw counts with the edgeR v4 model-fitting pipeline:

```r
edgeR::glmQLFit(dge, design, dispersion = NULL, robust = TRUE, legacy = FALSE)
```

TMMwsp normalization is calculated once. The full-rank design has one named
coefficient per batch and preserves the supplied group and covariates. For a
sample in a non-reference batch, only its batch indicators are changed to form
the reference counterfactual design. The QL fit coefficients and offsets define
the observed and counterfactual means.

The v4 pipeline estimates one global underlying negative-binomial dispersion.
That `nb_dispersion` supplies the dispersion for `pnbinom()`, `dnbinom()`, and
`qnbinom()`. Genewise `ql_dispersion` and `posterior_ql_dispersion` describe
residual quasi-likelihood variability and remain separate diagnostics.

For observed count $y$, the deterministic mid-P probability is

$$u=F_{NB}(y-1;\mu_{obs},\phi_{NB})+
\tfrac12P_{NB}(Y=y;\mu_{obs},\phi_{NB}).$$

The adjusted count is the NB quantile under the counterfactual reference mean
and the same valid global NB dispersion. Observed zeros remain zero. Genes that
are all zero in any batch are unsupported and returned unchanged. Transport is
performed by non-reference batch and gene chunk; intermediate means are not
retained in the result.

## Biologically adjusted reference scoring

An intercept-only within-batch model treats biological heterogeneity as
unexplained variability. When biological-group composition or supplied
covariates differ among batches, that can inflate a candidate's dispersion and
confound technical reference scoring with biological structure.

For each candidate batch, ComBat-refQL therefore constructs a fresh local
design from that batch's samples. The design always contains an intercept and
then adds the biological group and supplied covariates when they are locally
estimable. Unused factor levels are dropped and recorded. Locally constant,
redundant, or non-estimable terms are omitted, as are terms that would exhaust
the residual degrees of freedom. If no biological term can be retained, the
candidate uses an intercept-only fallback and records the reason.

Each valid candidate is fitted with

```r
edgeR::glmQLFit(
  local_dge,
  local_design,
  dispersion = NULL,
  robust = TRUE,
  legacy = FALSE
)
```

The candidate score is the valid global underlying NB dispersion returned by
that local edgeR v4 QL fit. The finite candidate with the smallest score is
selected unless the user supplies an explicit reference. Local QL and NB
dispersion quantities remain separate under the same boundary used for the
main model.

Automatic reference selection is a deterministic implementation score. The
candidate diagnostics retain the information needed to evaluate its behaviour
alongside study design and external quality-control evidence.
